brief.situation: You work on the staff helpdesk team at Tamsin Rail, a fictional train operator. Yesterday you deployed a chat model in the Microsoft Foundry portal and it answered in the playground. This morning you wrote a small Python chat client for a demo to the operations manager at 11:00. Every request fails with a 404.
handover: The endpoint and key are read from environment variables; the repository is shared with the whole team.
The demo question is 'Can I take a bicycle on the 07:12 to Harrowgate?'; the helpdesk's bicycle policy is in the brief you were given.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows your client, the Foundry project's endpoint and the model deployment.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

systemPrompt.label: Add a system message: helpdesk scope, two-sentence answers, the bicycle policy, say when unsure

effects.output: dev@laptop:~/helpdesk-chat$ (chat.py) messages=[{{"role": "system", "content": "You answer Tamsin Rail staff helpdesk questions. Use only the policy text below. Answer in at most two sentences. If the policy does not cover it, say so and give the helpdesk number. Policy: folding bicycles anytime; full-size bicycles off-peak only, not 07:00-09:30 on weekdays."}}, {{"role": "user", "content": question}}]

writeup.question: For the record: why the client got a 404, what you changed, and how you made the answers fit the helpdesk.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Reads the error code and compares the request with the deployment list.
parts.modelAnswer: 404 DeploymentNotFound with a valid key: the client sent model="gpt-4.1-mini", the model's name, but requests are routed by deployment name, and the portal deployment is called helpdesk-chat.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Uses the deployment name from configuration and keeps the key out of the code.
parts.modelAnswer: The client now reads the deployment name from AZURE_AI_DEPLOYMENT (helpdesk-chat); the endpoint and key stay in environment variables, not in the shared repository. A second deployment named after the model was not needed.

parts.label: Answers
parts.criteria: Shapes the answers with a system message and tests on and off topic.
parts.modelAnswer: A system message sets the helpdesk role, the policy text, a two-sentence limit and what to do when unsure; the demo question now gets the right short answer and an off-topic request is declined.

keyCommitted.headline: A secret in the history
keyCommitted.body: A 404 is not an authentication error; a wrong key gives 401. Keys belong in environment variables or Microsoft Entra ID authentication; a pushed key has to be regenerated.

demoFailed.headline: The demo hit a 404
demoFailed.body: New packages send the same request. The error said DeploymentNotFound; the deployment list shows the name to use.

ready.headline: Good: the right name, the right instructions
ready.body: You read the error code, compared the request with what the portal deployed, fixed the name through configuration, kept the key out of the code, and used a system message to make the answers fit the helpdesk, then tested both kinds of question.

scoring.modelReasoning: The request is accepted by the endpoint, so the key works; the 404 says the deployment named in the request does not exist. The deployment list shows the portal deployment is helpdesk-chat, while the code passes the model's name, gpt-4.1-mini, and requests are routed by deployment name. Read the deployment name from configuration rather than creating a duplicate deployment, and keep the key in the environment, never in a shared repository. Then add a system message that sets the helpdesk role, gives the policy text, limits length and says what to do when unsure, and test both the demo question and an off-topic one before 11:00.
